answer: Every epoch a public beacon assigns each key a unique storage shard derived from hash(address, epoch) plus a line from a published fable. During a randomly timed tide window, auditors request that exact shard; a miss or a collision (one disk answering for many keys) slashes a posted per-key bond. An N-key farm must keep N shards hot and answer N concurrent requests, so storage, bandwidth, and bond all scale per identity and cannot sit on one machine.
